rlw1.intro: The Breyer Ruy. The bishop retreats to a4, the knight reroutes via b8 to d7, and White finishes with the knight to f1.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
a6 asks the light-squared bishop a question. Black wants to know if White will trade or keep it.
Ba4 keeps the light-squared bishop. Retreating rather than taking keeps that bishop for later, and the pawn on d7 still stops a full pin.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king is safe before the centre opens.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling. It also defends the knight on f6.
Re1 puts the rook behind the pawn on e4, so that pawn is defended.
b5 attacks the bishop on a4 and gains queenside space.
Bb3 keeps the light-squared bishop and steps off the pawn. The diagonal toward f7 stays open.
d6 supports the pawn on e5 and frees the light-squared bishop. The centre stays closed.
c3 prepares a central pawn and gives the bishop a square to drop to.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
h3 stops a piece landing on g4 and gives the king air before the centre opens.
Nb8 starts the Breyer reroute. The knight leaves c6 so the c-pawn can move, and it is heading for d7.
d4 opens the centre at last. The preparation is done.
Nbd7 completes the reroute and supports the pawn on e5.
Nbd2 develops the queen's knight toward the kingside. The Spanish knight manoeuvre has started.
Bb7 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
Bc2 tucks the light-squared bishop back, ready for the kingside once the centre opens.
Re8 puts the rook on the e-file, behind the pawn on e5.
Nf1 continues the knight manoeuvre toward the kingside. From here the knight can go to g3.

rlw2.intro: The Arkhangelsk. Black fianchettos early, and White meets it with a quiet centre, a4, and the bishop on a2.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
a6 asks the light-squared bishop a question. Black wants to know if White will trade or keep it.
Ba4 keeps the light-squared bishop. Retreating rather than taking keeps that bishop for later, and the pawn on d7 still stops a full pin.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
b5 attacks the light-squared bishop and gains space before the dark-squared bishop comes out.
Bb3 keeps the light-squared bishop and aims toward f7.
Bb7 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal. This early fianchetto is the Arkhangelsk.
d3 supports the pawn on e4 and frees the dark-squared bishop. White stays solid against the fianchetto.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
a4 attacks the pawn on b5 and challenges the queenside expansion.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Re1 puts the rook behind the pawn on e4.
d6 supports the pawn on e5 and keeps the centre closed.
Nbd2 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Na5 attacks the bishop on b3. Black wants that bishop off its diagonal.
Ba2 keeps the light-squared bishop and steps off the knight. The diagonal toward f7 remains.

rlw3.intro: The Berlin. Queens come off, the black king steps to d8 and back, and White builds with the rook and the knight on e4.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4. Black does not ask the bishop a question first, so this is the Berlin.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The pawn on e4 is offered.
Nxe4 takes the pawn on e4. Black accepts the pawn, and the centre will open.
d4 attacks the pawn on e5 and opens lines while the king is already castled.
Nd6 attacks the bishop on b5 and drops the knight back into the centre.
Bxc6 takes the knight on c6. White damages the queenside pawns rather than save the bishop.
dxc6 recaptures the bishop on c6 and opens the d-file. The pawns are doubled.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and opens the centre. The knight on d6 is asked to move.
Nf5 steps the knight off the pawn and toward an active square.
Qxd8+ takes the queen on d8 and gives check. The Berlin endgame starts here.
Kxd8 takes the queen on d8 and gets out of check. The king is in the centre, which this line accepts.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and eyes the centre.
Ke8 steps the king back toward safety. It is not castling, but it leaves the d-file.
h3 gives the king air and takes g4 away from Black's pieces.
Be6 develops the light-squared bishop to a solid square.
Rd1 puts the rook on the open d-file. The king has stepped aside to e8.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and covers the king.
Ne4 plants the knight in the centre. The endgame play is about this knight and the open file.

rlw4.intro: The Open Defence. Black takes on e4, holds the centre with d5, and White builds with c3, the knight on d2, and the bishop on c2.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
a6 asks the light-squared bishop a question.
Ba4 keeps the light-squared bishop. Retreating rather than taking keeps that bishop for later.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The pawn on e4 can be taken.
Nxe4 takes the pawn on e4. This capture is the Open Defence.
d4 challenges the pawn on e5 and opens lines. White does not take the knight back at once.
b5 attacks the bishop on a4 and gains space.
Bb3 keeps the light-squared bishop on the diagonal toward the centre.
d5 plants a pawn in the centre and blunts the bishop on b3. The Open Defence is built on this pawn.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and opens the centre. The knight on e4 stays for the moment.
Be6 develops the light-squared bishop and challenges the bishop on b3.
c3 supports the centre and gives the light-squared bishop a retreat.
Bc5 develops the dark-squared bishop onto an active diagonal.
Nbd2 develops the queen's knight and challenges the knight on e4.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bc2 steps the light-squared bishop off the bishop on e6 and keeps it.
Nxd2 takes the knight on d2. Black removes the piece that was challenging the centre.
Qxd2 recaptures the knight on d2 and develops the queen.

rlw5.intro: The Exchange Ruy. White takes on c6, queens come off, and the knight lands on c4 against the bishop on d6.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
a6 asks the bishop on b5 a question. In this line White takes.
Bxc6 takes the knight on c6. White gives up the bishop pair to damage Black's pawns.
dxc6 recaptures the bishop on c6 and opens the d-file. The pawns are doubled.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
f6 supports the pawn on e5. The king's side is a little airy, which this structure accepts.
d4 opens the centre and attacks the pawn on e5.
Bg4 pins the knight on f3 to the queen on d1. The pin is real.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and opens the d-file. The queens now face each other.
Qxd1 takes the queen on d1. Black is happy to trade into the endgame.
Rxd1 recaptures the queen on d1. The rook arrives on the open file.
fxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and restores a pawn in the centre.
Rd3 lifts the rook. It can swing along the third rank and keep pressure.
Bd6 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the pawn on e5.
Nbd2 develops the queen's knight toward c4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight.
Nc4 attacks the bishop on d6 and the pawn on e5. That is the square the knight was heading for.

rlw6.intro: The Schliemann. Black strikes with the f-pawn, White's knights take in the centre, and the g-pawn recaptures before both sides castle.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
f5 is the Schliemann. Black challenges the pawn on e4 at once and accepts an open king's side.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e4. White meets the gambit with a piece.
fxe4 takes the pawn on e4 and opens the f-file.
Nxe4 recaptures the pawn on e4. The knight stands in the centre.
Nf6 attacks the knight on e4 and develops the king's knight.
Qe2 develops the queen and defends the knight on e4. She also eyes the e-file.
d5 attacks the knight on e4 and claims the centre.
Nxf6+ takes the knight on f6 and gives check.
gxf6 recaptures the knight on f6 and gets out of check. The king's side pawns are doubled.
d4 opens the centre against the pawn on e5.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal and prepares castling.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and opens lines.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. Black castles despite the doubled pawns.
Bxc6 takes the knight on c6 and damages the queenside as well.
bxc6 recaptures the bishop on c6. More doubled pawns, and the bishop on g7 stays.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. White castles once the tactics have settled.

rlw7.intro: The Classical Ruy with the bishop on c5. White opens the centre, the queen comes to d5, and then steps home once the knight has moved.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
Bc5 develops the dark-squared bishop and aims at the pawn on f2. This is the Classical, not the closed Ruy.
c3 prepares the central pawn push and takes b4 away from the bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
d4 attacks the bishop on c5 and opens the centre.
Bb6 keeps the dark-squared bishop and steps off the pawn.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and opens the centre. The new pawn attacks the knight on f6.
Nxe4 takes the pawn on e4. The knight jumps into the centre.
Qd5 attacks the undefended knight on e4. She also hits the knight on c6.
Nc5 steps the knight off the queen.
Bg5 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the queen on d8.
Ne7 steps the queen's knight in front of the queen and attacks the queen on d5.
Qd1 steps the queen off that knight and back home.

rlw8.intro: The Old Steinitz. Black plays d6, the centre opens, and White drops the bishop back to f1 before bringing the knight to f3.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the knight on c6. The pawn on d7 still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
d6 supports the pawn on e5 and keeps the position solid. This is the Old Steinitz, a little cramped.
d4 opens the centre at once. Against this passive pawn, White does not wait.
Bd7 develops the light-squared bishop and breaks the pressure on the knight on c6.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
Re1 puts the rook on the e-file.
exd4 takes the pawn on d4 and releases the centre.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4 and puts a knight in the centre.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bf1 brings the light-squared bishop home. White keeps it rather than trade it on c6.
Re8 puts the rook on the e-file.
Nf3 brings the knight back from d4, and the queen on d1 looks up the file at the pawn on d6.

rlw9.intro: The Bird Defence. The knight jumps to d4, White takes and castles, and the bishop comes to c4 before the centre is settled with d3.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the queen's knight. The pawn in front of the king still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
Nd4 is the Bird jump. The knight attacks the bishop on b5 and offers itself to be taken.
Nxd4 takes the knight on d4. White removes the jumper rather than moving the bishop.
exd4 recaptures the knight on d4. Black has a pawn in the centre.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king leaves before that pawn becomes a problem.
c6 attacks the bishop on b5 and supports the pawn on d4.
Bc4 steps the light-squared bishop off the pawn and aims at the pawn on f7.
Nf6 develops the king's knight.
Re1 puts the rook on the half-open e-file.
d6 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop.
c3 attacks the pawn on d4 and challenges the wedge.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and removes the wedge.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
d3 supports the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop. The position has settled into a normal open game.

rlw10.intro: The Marshall Gambit. Black gives a pawn for an attack, the queen comes to h4 and h3, and White meets it with g3, the bishop, and the queen.
notes: e4 opens the game and frees the light-squared bishop.
e5 meets White in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5.
Bb5 attacks the queen's knight. The pawn in front of the king still stands between that knight and the king, so this is pressure, not yet a full pin.
a6 asks the light-squared bishop a question.
Ba4 keeps the light-squared bishop. Retreating rather than taking keeps that bishop for later.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and attacks the pawn on e4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
Re1 puts the rook behind the pawn on e4.
b5 attacks the bishop on a4 and gains space.
Bb3 keeps the light-squared bishop and aims toward f7.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. Black castles before the gambit.
c3 prepares the central pawn. In the Marshall, Black strikes before that pawn arrives.
d5 offers a pawn to open lines against the castled king. This is the Marshall Gambit.
exd5 takes the pawn on d5 and accepts the gambit.
Nxd5 recaptures the pawn on d5 and plants the knight in the centre.
Nxe5 takes the pawn on e5. White collects the gambit pawn.
Nxe5 takes the knight on e5. The knights come off.
Rxe5 recaptures the knight on e5. The rook steps into the centre, which the attack will chase.
c6 attacks the knight on d5 and supports the centre. The attack needs this pawn move.
d4 supports the centre and opens a path for the dark-squared bishop.
Bd6 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the rook on e5. The rook should leave.
Re1 steps the rook off the bishop and back to the e-file.
Qh4 brings the queen out toward the king on g1. The attack has started.
g3 asks the queen a question and gives the king air. The pawn also blunts the bishop on d6.
Qh3 steps the queen off the pawn and attacks the pawn on h2.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and covers the kingside.
Bg4 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the queen on d1.
Qd3 steps the queen off the bishop and helps the defence.
Rae8 puts the other rook on the e-file. Both black rooks are now in the attack.
Nbd2 develops the queen's knight and finishes the book defence against the Marshall.
